title: WorkOS explorer
basis: WorkOS docs read on 2026-11-15; the pages show no date or version, so the read date is used.

levels.label: Team
levels.description: Your WorkOS account: the people who use the Dashboard, billing and the projects. It is not a customer of your app and holds none of your app's users.

levels.label: Project
levels.description: Groups the environments of one product. Every team starts with one project holding a staging and a production environment. Use a project for a fully separate setup, such as another product.

levels.label: Environment
levels.description: Staging or production, fully isolated. API keys, users, organizations, connections, webhook endpoints and branding are each scoped to one environment and do not carry over.

levels.label: Organization
levels.description: A customer (tenant) of your app. The top-level resource that SSO connections, directories and audit log events belong to. It has no limit on number. It reaches users only through memberships.

levels.label: User
levels.description: A person who signs in, identified by email address. The user belongs to the environment, not to an organization: one user can be a member of zero, one or many organizations.

objects.name: Dashboard members and roles
objects.summary: People who sign in to the WorkOS Dashboard, each with a role. A dashboard user can belong to only one team.
objects.note: Not the users of your app.

objects.name: Team authentication
objects.summary: Require MFA, set up SSO and provision dashboard accounts from your identity provider.

objects.name: Billing
objects.summary: Payment method, invoices and usage. Adding billing information unlocks the production environment.
objects.note: The Billing page sits with the team pages of the Dashboard docs but does not state its level in so many words.

objects.name: Feature flag definitions
objects.summary: Defined once for the project and shared by every environment in it.

objects.name: Audit Logs schema
objects.summary: The actions and targets your audit events may use, shared across the project's environments.

objects.name: Custom email domains
objects.summary: The sender domain for WorkOS emails, shared across the project's environments.

objects.name: API key and client ID
objects.summary: Your server's secret key (sk_...) to call WorkOS, with the client ID. In staging the key can be viewed again; in production it is shown once.
objects.note: Each application in an environment has its own client ID.

objects.name: Application
objects.summary: One client of your product (web, mobile or desktop). It has its own client ID, redirect URIs and sessions, and shares the environment's users. A default one exists.

objects.name: Branding
objects.summary: Logo, colours and theme of the hosted sign-in and the Admin Portal. Can be copied from another environment.

objects.name: Webhook endpoint
objects.summary: Where WorkOS sends events for this environment.

objects.name: Environment roles and permissions
objects.summary: Roles that apply across all organizations. An organization can add custom roles of its own.

objects.name: M2M application
objects.summary: Credentials for a customer's service to call your API (client credentials). The token carries an org_id claim for the organization granted access.
objects.note: The page says what it is for, not where it is configured; the environment is inferred.

objects.name: Pipes provider
objects.summary: A third-party service (GitHub, Slack, ...) you enable for users to connect. Set up in the Dashboard; an organization can override its scopes and credentials.
objects.note: The environment level is inferred from the Dashboard setup, not stated.

objects.name: Vault
objects.summary: Encrypted storage for secrets, with keys segmented by organization, user or any context you give.
objects.note: The docs describe the key context, not the level the store lives at.

objects.name: Domain
objects.summary: An email domain of the customer. It must be verified (by the Dashboard, the Admin Portal or DNS) before SSO works. A sign-in whose email does not match is rejected by default.

objects.name: SSO connection
objects.summary: The SAML or OIDC link between the organization and its identity provider. This is where SSO fits.

objects.name: Directory
objects.summary: A synced user directory (SCIM) with its directory users and directory groups. Separate from your app's users.

objects.name: Admin Portal link
objects.summary: A link that lets the customer's IT contact verify domains and set up SSO and Directory Sync themselves.
objects.note: The page describes the link; that it is made for one organization is inferred.

objects.name: Organization API key
objects.summary: A key owned by the organization to call your API, with permissions you allow. The secret is shown once, at creation.

objects.name: Custom role
objects.summary: A role defined for one organization only.

objects.name: FGA resource
objects.summary: A thing in your app that access is granted on. The organization is the root of the resource hierarchy; roles are assigned on resources.

objects.name: Audit log event
objects.summary: A record of an action (who, what, on what). Each event belongs to an organization.

objects.name: Organization membership
objects.summary: Links one user to one organization, with one or more roles. This is how a user is in an organization.
objects.note: Owned here, seen from the user as well.

objects.name: Shared Pipes connection
objects.summary: An administrator connects a provider once and shares it with every active member.

objects.name: User API key
objects.summary: A key owned by one member, limited to the permissions enabled for user keys. Managing all of an organization's user keys is a separate permission.

objects.name: Pipes connection
objects.summary: By default each user connects and owns their own third-party account.

objects.name: MFA factor
objects.summary: A second factor the signed-in user manages.

objects.name: Session
objects.summary: An active sign-in of the user, which can be listed and revoked.

keys.name: Environment API key
keys.use: Your backend calls the WorkOS API. One per environment; never in a browser or a mobile app.

keys.name: Organization API key
keys.use: The customer calls your API. Created by their admins with the API Keys widget, limited to permissions you allow.

keys.name: User API key
keys.use: A single person calls your API, with permissions enabled for user keys.

keys.name: M2M application
keys.note: The page says what it is for, not where it is configured; the environment is inferred.
keys.use: Server-to-server calls with client credentials; the token names the organization. The other way, next to API keys, to give customers programmatic access.
